svg.title: Harness Engine — portable execution architecture
svg.desc: Implemented request, session, event, and adapter paths · dashed = planned or optional · Dynamic Agents remains unchanged

text.tspan: Implemented request, session, event, and adapter paths · dashed = planned or optional · Dynamic Agents remains unchanged
Resolve runtime · enforce capabilities · no silent fallback
AG-UI / SSE · replay cursor · run ID
Existing checkpoints, memory, tools, and streams
Detached runs and durable canonical events
Provider SDK types stop at the adapter boundary
202 transfers execution ownership to Harness Engine
Subscriber disconnect does not cancel the provider task
Reconnect replays events after the last cursor
No user bearer token sent to provider
managed harness or custom runtime · deterministic runtimeSessionId
Bedrock-backed SDK profile · provider resume session ID
Mongo transcript mirror makes resume replica-independent
Planned: exclusive lease per session epoch · static operator profiles
RuntimeClass + resource limits + default-deny egress + short-lived capabilities
Provider SDK types and native state never enter the control-plane contract
All outward events use the canonical CAIPE lifecycle
AgentCore memory may back Claude SDK
Existing agent IDs and chat endpoints are preserved.
Agents without execution_harness_id remain on the unchanged
Dynamic Agents implementation of LangChain Deep Agents.
The BFF stays horizontally stateless. Harness Engine owns
provider work, durable session bindings, run state, and replayable
Portable services can mix providers, for example Claude SDK
